 Nov 16, 2026 How To Cut Your Student Loan Rate 1% by the Dec. 31 Deadline and Save Thousands
 A year and a half of savings on thousands awaits borrowers smart enough to claim this offer. Written by John Csiszar | Edited by Brendan McGinley Add us as a preferred source Thanks to a recent extension, student loan borrowers can cut their interest rate by a full percentage point by signing up for autopay.
 The rate drop will last all the way through June 30, 2028, potentially saving hundreds of dollars in interest for eligible borrowers. But the Dec. 31, 2026 deadline is coming up fast.

 How the 1% Student Loan Discount Works
 Historically, federal student loan borrowers were granted a 0.25% interest rate discount if they signed up for automatic payments. That discount quadrupled beginning July 1, 2026, when the U.S. Department of Education increased that reduction to a full percentage point. In response to that announcement, nearly 2 million borrowers enrolled in autopay over the summer, according to the department.
 The enhanced discount is only temporary and is set to expire on June 30, 2028, roughly two years after it went into effect. Borrowers must remain enrolled in autopay and continue repayment to keep receiving the benefit.
 Here's How Much You Could Save
 Loan savings will vary based on a number of factors, from the size of the outstanding loan balance to how quickly it is being paid off. 
 For example, consider someone with a $25,000 student loan carrying a 6% interest rate and 10 years remaining on a fixed repayment schedule . With the monthly payment remaining at approximately $278, reducing the interest rate to 5% for 20 months would save roughly $408 in interest between November 2026 and June 2028.
 Someone with a $50,000 loan balance with the same terms could save closer to $816.
 These calculations are representative only and make certain assumptions, such as monthly interest accrual and regular monthly payments. According to Federal Student Aid, 
 Not Every Federal Student Loan Qualifies
 The increased discount does not apply to all federal student loans . Specifically, older Direct Loans and loans under the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) or Perkins Loan programs don't qualify for the additional reduction.
 Federal Student Aid explained that the discount does apply to Direct Loans disbursed on or after July 1, 2012, and borrowers must remain in repayment throughout. That immediately excludes borrowers who are in deferment or forbearance. Borrowers in default, who must consolidate existing loans and enroll in new repayment plans before signing up for autopay, may not have time to qualify for the discount before the December deadline.
 How To Get the Discount Before Dec. 31
 You can enroll in the discount program for free, but you’ll have to do it through your federal student loan servicer, not the Education Department itself.
 All you have to do is log into your loan servicer's website, select the autopay option and provide the bank account information needed for automatic withdrawals.
 The deadline is 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on Dec. 31, 2026, per Federal Student Aid.
 If you’re already enrolled in autopay, you don’t have to sign up again. The Education Department said that if you’re still eligible, you’ll automatically receive the enhanced discount.
 One Thing To Consider Before Enrolling
 A lower interest rate doesn't necessarily mean a lower monthly student loan payment . If you’re on a Student Aid income-driven repayment plan , for example, your payments are generally based on your income and family size. The overall amount of interest you have to pay will go down, but it may not change your monthly payment amount.
 That doesn’t reduce the benefit of the program in any way. Borrowers carrying substantial federal student loan balances can see a significant reduction in their borrowing costs if they qualify and enroll before the deadline.
